set.body:
Scope

Use munit-scalacheck or an equivalent portable generator layer for the actual algebraic and metamorphic contracts. Do not create ceremonial law modules for ordinary bookkeeping.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deterministic generators cover explicit/mixed acquisition grids, causal kernels/bases, impulses/epochs, event tables, factor schemas/cells, modulators/missingness, censor segments, weights, rank/scale stress, and multiresponse matrices.
- [ ] Shrinking preserves validity constraints and reduces failures to scientifically intelligible counterexamples.
- [ ] HRF properties include causality/support, additivity, amplitude homogeneity, pulse partition/convergence, translation, basis permutation/transport, reconstruction, and normalization idempotence where applicable.
- [ ] Design properties include event-row permutation, term/column permutation equivariance, factor relabeling, structural origin stability, fingerprint sensitivity, and audit consistency.
- [ ] Fit properties include exact recovery, column scaling, WLS/known-GLS transformations, multiresponse decomposition, chunk invariance, fixed-effects associativity, and censor segmentation.
- [ ] Rank-deficient properties compare projection/fitted geometry and estimable functions, not arbitrary coefficients.
- [ ] Tolerances incorporate operation, scale, machine epsilon, and condition evidence rather than one globally loosened threshold.
- [ ] Seeds and failure replays are printed/recorded so a CI counterexample is reproducible.
- [ ] Suites run on JVM and Scala.js within an explicit PR-time budget; larger calibration cases have a separate lane.
set.title: P4.1: add generated computational laws and hostile-input shrinking
